'''Giuseppe Bagnera''' (14 November 1865 – 12 May 1927) was an Italian [[mathematician]].

==Biography==
At the University of Palermo, Bagnera received his ''laurea'' in civil engineering in 1890 and then his ''laurea'' in mathematics in 1895. His teachers included [[Giovanni Battista Guccia]], [[Francesco Gerbaldi]] ed [[Ernesto Cesàro]]. In 1899 he was appointed ''libero docente'' (lecturer) in algebraic analysis at the University of Palermo. He was appointed professor extraordinarius of infinitesimal calculus in 1901, then professor ordinarius in 1905, at the University of Messina, where he remained until the [[1908 Messina earthquake|1908 earthquake]]. He then taught at the University of Palermo until 1922 when he moved to the [[Sapienza University of Rome]], where he taught until his death.<ref name=MacBio>{{MacTutor Biography|id=Bagnera|title=Giuseppe Bagnera}}</ref><ref name=Treccani>[http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/giuseppe-bagnera_(Dizionario-Biografico)/ Bagnera, Giuseppi — Treccani, Dizionario-Biografico] {{in lang|it}}</ref><ref>[http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/giuseppe-bagnera/ Bagnera, Giuseppe, treccani.it] (entrata abbreviate) {{in lang|it}}</ref>

==Contributions==
He was an Invited Speaker, along with [[Michele de Franchis]], of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in April 1908 in Rome.<ref>{{cite book|author=Bagnera, G.|author2=de Franchis, M.|chapter=Sopra le equazioni algebriche F(X,Y,Z) = 0 che si lasciano risolvere con X,Y,Z funzioni quadruplamente periodiche di due parametri|editor=G. Castelnuovo|title=Atti del IV Congresso Internazionale dei Matematici (Roma, 6–11 Aprile 1908)|year=1909|volume=2|pages=242–248|chapter-url=http://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=miun.aag4063.0082.001;view=1up;seq=242}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Bagnera, G.|author2=de Franchis, M.|chapter= Intorno alle superficie regolari di genere uno che ammettono una rappresentazione parametrica mediante funzioni iperellitiche di due argomenti|editor=G. Castelnuovo|title=Atti del IV Congresso Internazionale dei Matematici (Roma, 6–11 Aprile 1908)|year=1909|volume=2|pages=249–256|chapter-url=http://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=miun.aag4063.0082.001;view=1up;seq=249}}</ref>

After the 1908 earthquake, Bagnera's publications included little research but consisted mainly of his lecture notes, which were of superb quality and polished to a high standard of clarity and accuracy.<ref>{{cite book|author=Virgopia, N.|chapter=Giuseppe Bagnera|title=Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani|volume=5|year=1963}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 1909, along with Michele de Franchis, Bagnera received the ''prix'' Bordin from the [[French Academy of Sciences]] for a work on [[hyperelliptic surface]]s. Bagnera was elected a member of the [[Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]] and was made an honorary professor of the [[Washington University in St. Louis]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://math.unipa.it/~brig/sds/prima%20pagina/tirocinio/Bagnera%20Giuseppe.htm |title=Giuseppe Bagnera, math.unipa.it |access-date=2017-11-19 |archive-date=2006-05-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060514012531/http://math.unipa.it/~brig/sds/prima%20pagina/tirocinio/Bagnera%20Giuseppe.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> His research dealt with [[finite group]]s, [[algebraic variety|algebraic varieties]], and [[abelian function]]s. His students include [[Michele Cipolla]], [[Pia Nalli]],<ref name=MacBio/> and [[Luciano Orlando]].
